title: Commit
description:
After staging a file in git, we can commit it.
A commit is just a point in time in the files history. It's how you save state in a repo, and how Git keeps track of changes. A commit comes with a message about what was changed.
Here is how you would commit all staged files:
```bash
git commit -m "Your commit message here"
```

---
## Assignment:
1. Commit `runthrough.md` with the message `A: add runthrough.md`
(Note you wouldn't normally letter commits, this is just for the course to allow easy identification.)
2. Run `git status` again and see the file is no longer staged.
Run and submit in the root directory.
